violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED RAITA AT 49-50F AND PEANUT SAUCE AT 49F IN THE TWO-DOOR UNDER-COUNTER; OBSERVED MILK AT 45F, HEAVY CREAM AT 51F, AND UNSALTED BUTTER AT 48F IN THE TWO-DOOR GLASS-FRONT COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED OF FOOD DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS COLD HOLDING FOODS NEED TO REMAIN AT 41F OR BELOW. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: OBSERVED TWO-DOOR UNDER-COUNTER COOLER AT 50F AND TWO-DOOR GLASS-FRONT COOLER AT 41F IN THE BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC DISCARDED OF TCS FOODS OUT OF TEMPERATURE AND MOVED ALL OTHER FOODS IN THE COOLERS. out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' PIC WAS UNABLE TO PROVIDE SIGNED COPIES OF POLICY.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS WILL EMAIL PIC COPIES OF POLICY.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS WILL EMAIL PIC COPY OF CLEAN UP PROCEDURE.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. OBSERVED NO EMPLOYEES WASH HANDS DURING INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE REVIEW HANDWASHING PROCEDURES WITH ALL OF STAFF.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED FRIED ONIONS MADE IN THE FACILITY KEPT AT AMBIENT TEMPERATURE; OBSERVED RAITA AT 48F, UNSALTED BUTTER AT 44F, AND YOGURT AT 45F IN THREE-DOOR UPR COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED OF ONIONS DURING INSPECTION AND MOVED OTHER FOOD ITEMS TO ANOTHER COOLER AS A PRECAUTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS ALL COLD HOLDING FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT 41F OR BELOW AT ALL TIMES. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED INCONSISTENT DATE MARKING SYSTEM IN PLACE.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC UNDERSTANDS FOOD ITEMS KEPT FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS SHOULD HAVE A DATE MARKING. PLEASE ENSURE DATE MARKING SYSTEM IMPROVES BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name

violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PLEASE ENSURE ALL FOOD ITEMS ARE LABELED PROPERLY.

violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: In-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED MULTIPLE IN-USE SPOONS IN A LARGE BUCKET WITH AMBIENT TEMPERATURE WATER BY THE STOVE.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED PROPER UTENSIL STORAGE. PIC REMOVED SPOONS FROM BUCKET AT TIME OF INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

violations.corrective_action: Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self- service is provided. PLEASE ENSURE UTENSILS ARE STORED WITH HANDLES UP TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION.

violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. PLEASE ENSURE THESE REFRIGERATORS ARE THOROUGHLY CLEANED BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHELLED EGGS STORED ABOVE READY-TO-EAT SAUCES IN THREE-DOOR UPR COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED EGGS DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS RAW MEATS SHOULD NEVER BE STORED ABOVE ANY READY-TO-EAT FOODS. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety foods are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours: OBSERVED CHICKEN BIRYANI 49F AND RICE AT 47-61F MADE THE EVENING PRIOR TO THE INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC DISCARDED FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PROPER COOLING METHODS WERE DISCUSSED WITH THE PIC AGAIN. PLEASE ENSURE COOLING FOODS ARE NOT STORED IN LARGE PORTIONS AND WITHOUT LIDS UNTIL THEY MEET 41F OR BELOW. Janatha Bar & Biryani (Inspection Date: 07/17/2025) Page 2 of 5

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: OBSERVED COOKED FROZEN SPINACH THAWING ON COUNTER-TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PROPER THAWING METHODS WERE DISCUSSED WITH THE PIC. PLEASE ENSURE STAFF ARE TRAINED ON PROPER THAWING PROCEDURES.

violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. PLEASE ENSURE ALL COLD HOLDING UNITS HAVE AN ACCURATE UNIT THERMOMETER.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: OBSERVED ONIONS DIRECTLY ON THE FLOOR IN THE BACK KITCHEN; OBSERVED CONTAINERS OF FOODS/BEVERAGES THROUGHOUT BACK KITCHEN AND WALK-IN COOLER STORED DIRECTLY ON THE GROUND.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PLEASE ENSURE ALL FOOD ITEMS ARE ELEVATED AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF THE GROUND TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION AND TO ALLOW FOR EASY CLEANING.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED CUPS STORED IN BULK FOOD ITEMS THROUGHOUT KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PLEASE DISCONTINUE USING CUPS FOR DISPENSING UTENSILS. ALL DISPENSING UTENSILS SHOULD HAVE A HANDLE IF THEY ARE STORED IN THE FOOD ITEM.

At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' PIC WAS UNABLE TO PROVIDE EHS WITH SIGNED COPIES OF THE EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS WILL EMAIL PIC MORE COPIES OF EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHRIMP AND RAW FISH STORED ABOVE VARIOUS PREPARED/COOKED ENTRÉES IN WALK-IN COOLER. OBSERVED RAW SHELLED EGGS STORED ABOVE VARIOUS SAUCES IN THE THREE-DOOR UPR COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC REORGANIZED COOLERS DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS RAW FOODS SHOULD BE STORED BELOW ANY READY-TO-EAT OR COOKED FOODS.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food items were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED FRIED CAULIFLOWER, MADE APPROXIMATELY 2 DAYS PRIOR TO INSPECTION, AT 44F IN WALK-IN COOLER. OBSERVED MILK DESSERT AT 49F AND APRICOT DESSERT AT 48F IN DISPLAY CASE.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED OF FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS COLD HOLDING FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT 41F OR BELOW.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED INCONSISTENT DATE MARKING SYSTEM FOR VARIOUS FOOD ITEMS PREPARED MORE THAN 24 HOURS PRIOR TO INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC UNDERSTANDS ALL PREPARED OR COOKED FOOD ITEMS KEPT FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS MUST HAVE A DATE MARKING. PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: OBSERVED COMMERCIALLY VACUUM PACKAGED TILAPIA THAWING IN WALK-IN COOLER IN INTACT PACKAGING.
violations.corrective_action: PIC REMOVED FISH FROM PACKAGING DURING INSPECTION AND UNDERSTANDS VACUUM PACKAGED FISH SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM PACKAGING OR THE PACKAGING SHOULD BE SLIT OPEN WHEN THE THAWING PROCESS BEGINS.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: OBSERVED 1-DOOR GLASS-FRONT COOLER AND FRONT DISPLAY CASE WITHOUT UNIT THERMOMETERS. WALK-IN COOLER THERMOMETER WAS OBSERVED AT 50F, WHICH IS INACCURATE.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. PLEASE ENSURE THESE UNITS HAVE ACCURATE THERMOMETERS BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: OBSERVED VARIOUS CONTAINERS AND BOTTLES OF FOODS (NOT ORIGINAL CONTAINERS) WITHOUT LABELS.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PLEASE ENSURE ANY FOOD ITEMS NOT IN ORIGINAL PACKAGING ARE LABELED.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor: OBSERVED VARIOUS CONTAINERS OF FOODS ON FLOOR OF WALK-IN COOLER; OBSERVED BAGS OF ONIONS AND RICE STORED ON THE FLOOR IN BACK KITCHEN STORAGE AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. PIC UNDERSTANDS ALL FOOD ITEMS SHOULD BE ELEVATED OFF THE GROUND TO ALLOW FOR EASY CLEANING AND TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. PIC WILL BE INSTALLING MORE SHELVING FOR BETTER STORAGE PRACTICES. PLEASE ENSURE CORRECTION BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: OBSERVED THE DISPLAY CASE AT 49F WITH EHS THERMOMETER.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC UNDERSTANDS NO TCS FOODS SHOULD BE STORED HERE UNTIL THE UNIT CAN MAINTAIN TEMPERATURES BETWEEN 34-38F. TCS FOODS IN THIS UNIT WERE DISCARDED DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed that the end caps are missing from the protective light covering of fluorescent light fixtures in the BACK KITCHEN NEAR THE TWO-DOOR UPR GLASS-FRONT COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Provide end caps to completely enclose the light bulb. PIC UNDERSTANDS ALL LIGHTS SHOULD BE SHIELDED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.
